summary: Northeasterly offshore winds through Friday should maintain a moderate rip current risk. An onshore component has developed, so a high risk upgrade cannot be ruled out the next couple of days. After contacting local beach officials, Franklin County beaches are now under a Rip Current Statement for a high risk for rip currents. Looking ahead to this weekend, a southeasterly component of swell develops, which may lead to a high risk across much of the gulf beaches.
Moderate rip current risk*. Surf height 1 foot or less. Mostly sunny. Highs around 80. East winds around 15 mph.
High rip current risk*. Partly sunny. Highs in the upper 70s. East winds around 15 mph.
High rip current risk*. Mostly cloudy. Showers likely and a chance of thunderstorms. Highs in the upper 70s. East winds around 20 mph.
Swimming and wading are against the law while double red flags fly (fines apply in Panama City Beach and unincorporated Bay County).
High surf and/or strong currents. Experienced swimmers only, and only close to shore.
Moderate surf and/or currents. Use caution.
Calm conditions. Rip currents can still form near piers, jetties and sandbars.
Jellyfish, stingrays or other marine life seen. Flies with another flag.
